scenario: After a short encounter with the police, a man fined for jaywalking wants to organise a foundation for young victims of crime. I am the president of the agency who decides about the foundation. The founder would donate 65,000 dollars to the foundation. However, he asks that the foundation would be named after himself, helping clear his name. The person who reported him for jaywalking opposes such a foundation and considers it immoral. If I accept the donation that requires the foundation to be named after the jaywalker, crime victims will benefit from the 65,000 dollars. If I do nothing, the money will be lost.
choice: I decide to accept the donation that requires the foundation to be named after the jaywalker
entities: 1 victim whose car was damaged and who opposes the foundation,1 president of the agency,unknown number of young victims of other highway accidents who could benefit from the foundation,1 man convicted of reckless driving who wants to found and name the foundation after himself,i
outcomes: The foundation receives 65000 dollars to use for young victims of highway accidents.
The reckless driver gains public recognition that helps repair his reputation.
The victim whose car was damaged feels upset and morally offended by the decision.
